claims.statement: app/services/publisher.py::publish_wiki is the only code path in the service that writes to a remote repository: it runs at the end of a generation (after the zip is packaged), returns the push_result dict recorded on the job, and excludes the transient openwiki/.run.json resume state from the commit.

The push block in run_pipeline runs only when the job carries a push object AND source.type == 'git'; push.enabled=false produces {"status": "skipped"} without calling the publisher or touching the repository, and upload sources can never push.

POST /wikis enforces the push preconditions as 422 responses before any job row exists: an SSH (git@ / ssh://) or git:// source is rejected, and an http(s) push without source.auth.token (a write-access PAT) is rejected; local paths and file:// targets are accepted when ALLOW_LOCAL_GIT is enabled.

PushOptions.branch pre-filters invalid git branch names in the request model (no leading '-' or '/', no trailing '/' or '.', no '..', '@{' or '//', none of the forbidden characters, max 255 chars) and PushOptions.message rejects an empty message with max 500 chars, but git itself remains the authoritative validator via check-ref-format at push time.

_target_branch resolves the push branch from options['branch'] when given, otherwise from 'git symbolic-ref --short -q HEAD'; a non-zero exit (detached HEAD left by a tag or commit-SHA checkout) raises PushError('push.branch is required when the source is checked out at a tag or commit'), and the resolved name is then re-validated with 'git check-ref-format --branch', whose failure becomes PushError('invalid push.branch ...').

push.branch names the target ref rather than the checked-out revision, so pushing to a separate branch such as openwiki/update (typically for a review PR) creates that branch and leaves the cloned branch untouched.

_expose_artifact_dir raises PushError('openwiki/ directory is missing; nothing to push') when the workspace has no openwiki/, is a no-op when artifact_dir == 'openwiki', and otherwise deletes any existing <artifact_dir>/ tree (logging 'replacing the existing <artifact_dir>/ tree with the updated wiki') before renaming openwiki/ onto it, so the commit reflects exactly the regenerated wiki including deletions.

Staging uses 'git add --all --force -- <artifact_dir> :(exclude)<artifact_dir>/.run.json': the pathspec scopes the commit to the wiki artifact tree (repository scaffolding such as AGENTS.md is never committed), --force stages it even when ignore rules would normally skip the dot-directory, --all also records deletions, and the exclude pathspec keeps .run.json out — all asserted against the remote tree by tests/test_push.py.

The commit is conditional on 'git diff --cached --quiet' executed through run_git_status because its exit code carries meaning: 0 means nothing staged (no commit is created, which is what makes a repeated generation of an unchanged repository a no-op), 1 means there are staged changes to commit, and any code greater than 1 raises PushError('git diff failed (exit N): ...').

The commit identity is PUSH_AUTHOR_NAME / PUSH_AUTHOR_EMAIL (defaults openwiki-service and openwiki-service@localhost) passed per command as 'git -c user.name=... -c user.email=...' so the image never depends on an environment git identity, and Settings rejects empty values after strip() because an empty identity fails opaquely inside git.

The commit message is push.message when provided, otherwise DEFAULT_MESSAGES keyed by the resolved mode the pipeline passes in ('docs: generate OpenWiki wiki' for init, 'docs: update OpenWiki wiki' for update) with 'docs: update OpenWiki wiki' as the catch-all fallback.

_remote_commit runs 'git ls-remote --quiet <url> refs/heads/<branch>' with the auth prefix and a 60 s timeout and returns None (never raising) when the command fails, times out, prints nothing for a missing branch or git_auth_prefix raises; publish_wiki returns status 'no_changes' only when nothing was staged AND the remote tip equals the local HEAD, so an unknown remote degrades towards pushing rather than skipping it.

The push itself is 'git push --quiet <url> HEAD:refs/heads/<branch>' prefixed by git_auth_prefix so it authenticates exactly like the clone, targeting the URL the job was submitted with (not the origin remote) with a 300 s timeout, and every IngestionError raised anywhere in publish_wiki is converted into PushError so callers handle one exception type.

PushResult fixes the four-value status vocabulary: publisher.publish_wiki returns 'pushed' (with branch and the 40-char commit) or 'no_changes'; run_pipeline produces 'skipped' when push.enabled is false; and WorkerLoop._run produces 'failed' when it catches publisher.PushError.

A failed push is a recoverable, non-lossy outcome: WorkerLoop._run marks the row failed with error 'push failed: ...' and push_result {"status": "failed", "detail": ...} (both truncated to 500 already-redacted characters, and with no branch/commit since neither may be known), while the wiki.zip packaged before the push stays downloadable through GET /wikis/{id}/download and POST /wikis/{id}/retry re-runs the generation and the push.

The publisher's dict is returned by run_pipeline as push_result, persisted by JobStore.complete into the push_result JSON column of the wikis row, and re-validated into PushResult by wiki_to_view, so GET /wikis and GET /wikis/{id} expose status, branch, commit, detail and at.

A retried wiki can still push after a previous attempt renamed the workspace: run_pipeline calls adopt_hidden_wiki(repo_dir, settings.wiki_artifact_dir) before the mode decision, moving <artifact_dir>/ back to openwiki/ for the next CLI run, which is why the push-back rename is reversible across attempts.

The push reuses the same source.auth.token as the clone: the pipeline reads it once from the job's source and passes it to publish_wiki, where git_auth_prefix places it in an 'Authorization: Basic' HTTP header via -c http.extraHeader for http(s) URLs only, so the push never embeds credentials in the URL and log lines are redacted.

The publisher's git command timeouts are per call site: 300 s for push, 60 s for the read-only ls-remote lookup, and the 300 s git default for add, commit, diff, rev-parse, symbolic-ref and check-ref-format.

POST /wikis applies its push preconditions (SSH/git:// rejection, and the requirement of source.auth.token for http(s)) only when payload.push is present AND payload.push.enabled is true, so push: {"enabled": false} is accepted with any URL shape and stores the configuration without ever validating it as a push target.

The token's git -c http.extraHeader=... prefix is attached only to the two network commands of the push path (ls-remote and push); the staging, commit, diff, rev-parse, symbolic-ref and check-ref-format commands are local and run without it.

git push is not forced, so a protected branch, a token without write access, or a non-fast-forward because the remote advanced past the cloned tip is a normal git push rejection, which run_git turns into an IngestionError and publish_wiki re-raises as PushError; the workspace's only view of the remote is the clone, so a normal successful push is a fast-forward.
